title: Mini Project
description: Check that you know how the full pipeline fits together before you run it yourself.

lessons.title: Start with the question
lessons.lead: A project without a question produces charts nobody asked for.

questions.prompt: Which is a usable project question?
options: "Which product category drove the drop in Q2 revenue?"
questions.explain: A good question names what you are comparing and can be answered from columns you actually have.

questions.prompt: How many questions should a mini project carry?
options: One main question and at most three supporting ones
As many as the dataset can answer
Exactly one, with no supporting questions
One per column in the dataset
questions.explain: Write the main question in the first markdown cell and keep it visible. Everything in the notebook should serve it.

questions.prompt: What should you write down before starting the analysis?
options: A one-sentence hypothesis — what you expect the answer to be
The conclusion you intend to present
The list of charts you will build
The libraries you plan to import
questions.explain: A stated expectation makes it obvious when the data disagrees with you, which is the interesting case.

lessons.title: Steps 1 and 2 — load, look, and clean
lessons.lead: Understand the shape and quality of the data before you change any of it.

questions.prompt: Which checks belong in the first cell after loading?
questions.explain: Exporting comes last. First understand what you loaded — size, types, gaps, and duplicates.

questions.prompt: Why keep the original file at `data/raw.csv` and write to `data/clean.csv`?
options: You will need to redo the cleaning at least once
Pandas cannot overwrite a file it has open
CSV files degrade when written repeatedly
questions.explain: Cleaning is a rerunnable script from raw to clean. Overwriting the raw file makes that impossible.

questions.prompt: What must accompany every cleaning decision?
options: A markdown cell saying why you made it
A backup copy of the DataFrame
questions.explain: An analysis that silently discards 40% of the data is not trustworthy. Report how many rows you dropped and why.

questions.prompt: Which line normalises messy column names?
questions.explain: Strip the whitespace, lowercase, and replace spaces — after that every column is reachable without guessing.

lessons.title: Steps 3 and 4 — answer it, then show it
lessons.lead: Aggregate toward the question you wrote down, and give each finding one chart.

questions.prompt: How many charts should the report carry?
options: Three to five — one per finding
As many as you produced while exploring
questions.explain: More charts than findings means you are showing your process rather than your conclusions.

questions.prompt: What is the test of whether an aggregation belongs in the report?
options: It maps to a sentence you can say out loud
It runs in under a second
questions.explain: If you cannot state what the number means, the reader will not work it out for you.

questions.prompt: Which chart carries the headline metric over time?
questions.explain: Time on the x axis, the metric on the y axis. Sorted bars are for comparing categories; a histogram is for one column's distribution.

lessons.title: Step 5 — the notebook as a report
lessons.lead: A reader who skips every code cell should still get the whole story.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of sections in the notebook?
questions.explain: State what you set out to answer, what you had to work with, what you changed, what you found, and what it means.

questions.prompt: What is the last thing to do before submitting?
options: Kernel ▸ Restart & Run All, so it runs top to bottom
questions.explain: A notebook that fails on restart is one of the most common sources of lost marks.

questions.prompt: Why state the limitations of your data?
options: Naming what the data cannot show makes the parts it does show more credible
It is required by the file format
It excuses mistakes in the analysis
questions.explain: Honest scoping is a mark of a careful analyst, not a weakness in the work.

questions.prompt: Which are required deliverables for this project?
options: `project.ipynb` that runs clean from a restarted kernel
A 5-minute walkthrough of question, method, and findings
The raw dataset uploaded to a public site
questions.explain: Marking weights: cleaning 25%, analysis 30%, charts 25%, presentation 20%.
